equity.level_reason: Race/ethnicity and sex prevalences are reported and contrasted with significance statements and values, but no contrast is computed as a difference or ratio, so the level is capped at 2; the editorial names social and cultural factors without quantifying the gap.

level_alternative.reason: A reader may count the reported black-white and sex contrasts with CIs as quantified contrasts, which would make the level 3.

equity.equity_measurement: Race/ethnicity limited to white, black and Hispanic students because other groups were too small; weights adjust for oversampling of black and Hispanic students, and the report does not compute race-specific differences.

notes: Significance is defined as non-overlapping 95% CIs, which is not a test, although the methods also cite a p less than 0.05 level. Survey weighting is the only procedure; there is no regression, adjustment or formal test. Sex and race contrasts are reported separately within middle and high school, so stratified/adjusted is recorded as within-level comparison without adjustment.
view_issues: The methods say significance is judged at 'pless than 0.05' (a garbled p-value threshold) yet define significance as non-overlapping 95% CIs; the CSV gives CIs as '±' half-widths, not bounds.
